text:
alen: Quick follow-up on telemetry attribute segmentation — we need clear guidance on what belongs in the "session-hot" bucket vs the "profile-sticky" bucket. This drives retention, index strategy, and cost attribution.

mira: +1. We keep hitting expensive queries because too many fields are treated as indexed. We should codify which attributes are query hot and which are purely billing/identity. :thinking_face: 

tj: Proposal sketch: split attributes into three tiers — hot-search, mid-rollup, sticky-id.
```
hot-search: trace_id, request_id, route, status_code
mid-rollup: feature_flag, experiment_id, release_tag
sticky-id: tenant_id, customer_tier, billing_key
```

kavi: I like tiers. A few tradeoffs:
- hot-search needs low-latency access (in-memory or fast index) -> higher cost
- mid-rollup can be materialized as daily aggregates -> cheaper
- sticky-id can be attached at ingest and scrubbed for PII retention policies

mira: Important: cost attribution needs tenant/billing_key available even if we sample spans. So sticky-id must survive sampling.

alen: Agreed. Also want to limit cardinality explosion from free-form attributes (user_agent, sdk_version). We should have a whitelist and a passive-telemetry flag to drop high-cardinality keys by default.

obs-bot: Note: RFC-3107 (attr-segmentation) draft posted. Please tag decisions here for cross-ref.

tj: Operational questions: if we move some resolution to the edge (edge-agent attaches tenant/billing_key), we reduce late-enrich joins but increase trust boundary. Thoughts?

kavi: Edge attach is great for latency but we need signing and attestation. Otherwise admins can't trust billing keys and we'll have to do backfill reconciliation.

mira: Another option: attach a short-lived routing token at edge and resolve to billing_key in a dedicated low-latency lookup service during ingest. Pros: smaller trust surface. Cons: additional lookup load and availability target.

alen: For now, pragmatic plan:
1) Define explicit attribute whitelist per tier (hot/mid/sticky).
2) Edge emits routing token + minimal sticky fields (tenant_id) — full billing_key resolved at ingest via lookup service.
3) Sampling rule: always keep sticky-id for sampled traces used for cost attribution.
4) Add a config flag to drop high-cardinality fields (default ON).

tj: Sounds good. Can we add a lightweight schema marker on the envelope: "attr_tier": ["hot","mid","sticky"] so downstream processors can fast-path without expensive schema introspection?

kavi: Yes. We'll need to version that marker. Also ensure it doesn't bloat payloads (single byte codes).

mira: Danger: backfills and historical queries. If we change tiers later, queries that relied on hot indices might break. We need a migration/playbook.

alen: ACTIONS:
- @mira to draft whitelist and cardinality heuristics (due EOW)
- @kavi to prototype routing-token -> billing_key lookup (P0 spike, 2w)
- @tj to sketch ingest pipeline marker and compact encoding (this week)
- infra: add feature flag to drop high-card keys at edge (toggleable per-customer)

mira: I'll include examples and a suggested retention policy per tier (hot = 7d, mid = 30d aggregated, sticky = 365d masked).

kavi: Note on query cost: we'll expose a tenant-visible cost-estimate when a query touches hot indices. Might help users opt for rollups.

obs-bot: Reminder: add RFC link to the ticket and set reviewers from billing + sre.

alen: Thanks all. If no objections, I'll land the attr-tier marker + whitelist RFC patch tomorrow and start the spike coordination. :thumbsup:

mira: No objections from me. :+1:

tj: Go for it.

kavi: SGTM.
